I think Bits Passats' feedback was appropriately delivered, remaining constructive whilst not mincing any words, and is appropriate to deliver publicly.

The OP has made just one post on this forum, which essentially dumped this translation effort and two screenshots with the very minimum of explanation or narrative. This comes in the wider context of a large number of AI-enabled projects landing on the forum, many of which have questionable quality.

Bits Passats is totally within rights to publicly suggest a higher bar. Anyone (including the OP) who takes note might then get the measure in future about what standard of contributions are likely to elicit encouragement from the community, and what are likely to elicit criticism, constructive or otherwise.

Aranya wrote
Hi, I'd like to share my opinion on this.

I think AI has democratised access to hacks, translations, game development, and so on. In my opinion, this is fantastic, but it also leads to a significant increase in the number of projects and, consequently, a decrease in their average quality.

Rather than rejecting or looking down on projects simply because they were made using AI, I think we could do EXACTLY THE SAME as we would with a manually created project: give the author feedback to encourage them to improve it and share our points of view.


Hello Aranya,

My piece of advice... do never let AI carelessly process without supervision sensible information, such as symbols. Symbology is a very powerful tool, but when misused it brings problems.

I am not looking down. I said exactly what it was wrong and why.

And everything revolves around a blatant lack of supervision of the process and its results.

Have a nice day

item.title: Main :: RE: The 20 Best SMS Games (according to Sega Retro)
item.description:
Author: kusfo
Posted: Thu Oct 29, 2026 1:44 pm (GMT 1.00)

baude wrote
kusfo wrote

Actually, and this may surprise a lot of people, but I've explained it some other times with other audiences, Popolous for SMS has the best controls of all versions, Amiga and PC included, and considering that no content was cut, that makes it the best version for playing Popolous, on any platform.

"What are you saying Kusfo? a strategy game is always better with a mouse". Well, that it's with modern UIs etc, but the Amiga version for instance, have two problems:

    - You have to navigate in and out of the playing field to different sides of the screen, with a terribly slow cursor
    - The cursor has the famous problem that you have to click in very specific parts of the elements to have the click succeed.


Instead, the Master System version allows you to move from field to the specific options with just one button, very fast (Something that the Megadrive version didn't copy).


I’m with you: I played the Master System version until I was completely worn out—getting past world 2.000 without cheats, and past world 5.000 with them—spending hundreds of hours on it. I thought it was a spectacular game, even before I had the chance to compare it to other versions. I realize it wasn’t the best platform, nor the ideal time, for people to enjoy a game like this, but I certainly did—so much so that a friend and I became huge Populous fans (all thanks to that Master System version). We both later tried the Mega Drive and Amiga versions: while they were certainly more visually impressive, the Master System version was far more enjoyable to play.


twin souls! <3
